content.title: Lyric Performance | Stable Performer and Line-by-Line Semantic Lift
content.summary: Hold identity through one continuously recognizable original performer. Give every lyric line readable type and a graphic action that matches its meaning, escalating camera, layout, and ensemble energy line by line. After the final proof, reduce text density and let the performer own the closing release.

quick_start.input_format: stable original performer + three or four original lyric lines + semantic graphic behavior per line + continuously readable identity + line-by-line escalation + text-cleared performance release
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult man with a silver buzz cut wears a mustard utility jacket and carries a black microphone along an inspection line. MARK THE PULSE appears accurately at his feet while four signal-cyan route markers light in sequence. He raises the microphone toward a closed maintenance door; OPEN THE CIRCUIT bends into a signal-cyan arc and the door opens outward along it. Clear the lyrics, leaving only four small cyan route markers. The same performer enters the bright center line, lowers the microphone, completes one full shoulder-and-arm phrase, and receives a synchronized work-light response from background workers.
required_anchors: Introduce one stable original performer, performance tool and first lyric in the same readable opening relation.
Give each lyric line exact readable copy and one distinct motion or spatial behavior derived from its meaning.
Use graphic elements to expand the performance space without covering the face, hands or primary action.
After the last lyric proof, reduce text density and end on a longer performer-led movement release.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Hold identity through one continuously recognizable original performer. Give every lyric line readable type and a graphic action that matches its meaning, escalating camera, layout, and ensemble energy line by line. After the final proof, reduce text density and let the performer own the closing release.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Keep one original performer continuously identifiable while each short lyric line appears with accurate readable typography and one graphic behavior derived from its meaning. Raise energy line by line through camera proximity, repeated figures, spatial graphics or audience scale, but never let text obscure the face or replace the performer. After the final lyric proof, reduce copy density and let the same performer carry a longer movement release. The reusable mechanism is performer-anchored semantic lyric escalation, not the source singer, lyrics, vector surface, wardrobe or exact layouts.

invariants.rule: Introduce one stable original performer, performance tool and first lyric in the same readable opening relation.
invariants.purpose: Binds identity to the lyric system immediately.
invariants.ablation_failure: Text without a performer becomes a title reel; a performer without text loses the lyric premise.

invariants.rule: Give each lyric line exact readable copy and one distinct motion or spatial behavior derived from its meaning.
invariants.purpose: Turns lyrics into visible action rather than subtitles.
invariants.ablation_failure: Generic bouncing text or misspelling weakens semantic proof.

invariants.rule: Keep the performer traceable through every lyric phase while increasing at least one energy channel per line.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing performers or increasing everything at once breaks continuity and legibility.

invariants.rule: Use graphic elements to expand the performance space without covering the face, hands or primary action.
invariants.ablation_failure: Foreground type that masks the body destroys the anchor.

invariants.rule: After the last lyric proof, reduce text density and end on a longer performer-led movement release.
invariants.purpose: Pays off the accumulated energy through character action.
invariants.ablation_failure: Another dense card at the end prevents performance closure.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source illustrated female singer, long braids, oversized pink sunglasses, microphone, jewelry and blue-gray outfit
the source exact lyrics Follow my steps, Catch the rhythm, Start a wave and One by one
the source pink-orange-blue vector palette, crowd, arrows, numbered ladder and radial paint fields
the source exact lyric timing, layouts, camera angles and semantic graphic assignments
the source creator's image and audio reference package and any source music or voice identity
